source.title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis

accepted.question_text: Let (A, ≺) be a partially ordered set equipped with its interval topology. Suppose every closed interval [a,b] = {x : a ⪯ x ⪯ b} is compact in that topology. Must (A, ≺) then be bicontinuous in the domain-theoretic sense, meaning that the way-below relation is characterized both by directed suprema and dually by filtered infima, with each upper set ↑x filtered and having infimum x? More broadly, is there an order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime result that compact causal diamonds imply causality in non-compact spacetimes of dimension greater than 2, and if so what should play the role of the dimensional hypothesis for posets, or does no such restriction arise in the purely order-theoretic setting?
accepted.context_brief: Compact intervals versus bicontinuity in posets

evidence.quote: Question 1: Consider a globally hyperbolic poset (A, ≺). Does the compactness of the intervals [a, b], under the interval topology, imply the bicontinuity of (A, ≺), in a similar fashion that the compactness in the closed diamonds in a spacetime M, under the Alexandrov topology TA, implies the (strong) causality of M (for dimensions strictly greater than 2)?

The only problem, towards [16], of considering a globally hyperbolic poset, is that we are left only with an order-theoretic structure; what would be, if there is such, the equivalent condition in [16] of “dimension strictly greater than 2”? Is there a possibility that the condition on the dimension applies only to globally hyperbolic spacetimes, while the proposed conjecture holds in globally hyperbolic posets without any restriction?

accepted.question_text: Is there a spacetime topology, different from the usual manifold topology and from the previously studied alternatives, that is both mathematically fruitful and physically meaningful? If such a topology exists, what criteria should govern its choice, and in particular how should it interact with a foliation of spacetime?

evidence.quote: Question 2: As we have seen in this section, there are many different candidates for spacetime topologies is, other than the manifold one. Is there a fruitful4 and physically meaningful spacetime topology that was not considered so far? What are the criteria for choosing it? For example, how should such a topology be related to the foliation of a spacetime?

These questions certainly need a more systematic work, because even if they can touch important problems (for example the singularity problem in relativity theory as well as Penrose’s cosmic censorship conjecture), they seem underestimated until now.

accepted.question_text: Can the topology of a spacetime be reconstructed in a rigorous technical way from the topology of an interval domain, as suggested by the equivalence between globally hyperbolic posets and interval domains? Relatedly, does the fact that candidate causal spacetime topologies such as the Zeeman fine topology, Göbel’s generalization, and the Hawking-King-McCarthy topology are non-metrizable reveal what kind of non-manifold topology should be regarded as the right topology for spacetime when the underlying model is order-theoretic?
accepted.context_brief: Recovering spacetime topology from interval domains

evidence.quote: Question 3: In the light of Theorem 3.8, we ask whether the topology of a spacetime can be reconstructed, in some technical and rigorous way, from the topology of an interval domain.

The spacetime topologies that we have mentioned in this section, like for example the Zeeman fine topology or its generalization by Göbel, or the one by Hawking-King-McCarthy are not metrizable; does this give us any insight on the appropriate candidate for a spacetime topology (other than the manifold topology), given that interval domains are order-theoretic objects?

accepted.question_text: For a general non-stationary globally hyperbolic spacetime, after conformally rewriting the metric in the form g̃ = -dt² + g̃Σ,ij(t,x) dxi dxj, does global hyperbolicity impose enough geodesic-completeness structure on each spatial slice (Σ_t, g̃Σ_t) to imply essential self-adjointness of the spatial Klein-Gordon or Laplace-type operator L(t)? Equivalently, outside the static, warped-product, and uniformly controlled sliced-space settings already understood in the paper, what precise relation remains between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian spacetime and geodesic completeness of the associated Riemannian hypersurfaces?
accepted.context_brief: Global hyperbolicity versus self-adjointness in non-stationary spacetimes

evidence.quote: In the case of non-stationary spacetimes, however, the connection between global hyperbolicity and self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian is still unclear.
Our strategical reason for the conformal transformation is our interest in the connection of global hyperbolicity and the geodesic completeness of the Riemannian manifold (Σt, g˜Σt) for all t ∈ R.

In general however, i.e. apart from the three classes discussed above, there is no direct connection between geodesic completeness of the hypersurfaces and global hyperbolicity the Lorentzian manifold5.
